messages.content:
You are evaluating a PTSD case vignette for the presence of causal
connections between five Ehlers & Clark cognitive components: Triggers, Negative Appraisals, Memory,
Threat, and Maladaptive Strategies.

For each of the 20 ordered, directed (A -> B) pairs of distinct components, decide whether the
vignette conveys, in some paragraph, that A influences, drives, or leads to B. Apply the same
causal standard as a structural validator:

COMPONENT SYNONYMS (any of these synonyms count as the component appearing):
  Triggers              -> "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals   -> "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory                -> "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat                -> "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies-> "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "safety behaviours", "maladaptive coping"

CAUSAL STANDARD
An edge A -> B is PRESENT (return 1) iff, within the same paragraph:
  (i) both A and B (or their synonyms) appear; AND
  (ii) the paragraph conveys that A influences / drives / leads to B, through direct causal
       language, sequential structure, or connecting phrases like "because of", "this meant",
       "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
If no paragraph conveys the A -> B relationship, return 0 for that edge.

You will return a binary judgement for each of the 20 ordered pairs. Be strict: do not assume
an edge based on mere co-occurrence; the paragraph must actually convey directional influence.

Evaluate the following vignette and judge each of the 20 directed edges
(A -> B) on whether the vignette conveys A influencing B.

VIGNETTE
The incident unfolded on a rain-slicked service road behind the veterinary hospital where Samir worked the night shift. A stranger had stepped from the shadows of the ambulance bay, pressing a knife against his ribs while the engine's diesel fumes and the mugger's sour breath flooded the alley. When Samir had frozen, he had felt the cold metal and the sudden, violent violation of his personal space. That moment of terror became the anchor for everything that followed. Over the next few weeks, the assault refused to stay contained. The olfactory recall would strike without warning in the exam room when a client's cheap cologne or the antiseptic cleaner caught the breeze, instantly dragging Samir back to the alley. When trying to explain the breakdown to his partner, Samir would lose the thread entirely, hands trembling as the narrative fractured. This involuntary memory intrusion directly fed his negative appraisals; each unbidden flashback convinced him he had permanently lost his happiness and that he could no longer rely on others to keep him safe. Consequently, his constant vigilance took over. He found himself scanning every crowded street for threatening postures and checking behind him whenever footsteps echoed, even at home where he felt perpetually alert and trapped. His professional environment quickly became a minefield. During a routine surgery, a sudden drop in a medical instrument's metal tray triggered a full somatic memory of the mugger's grip. The threat system hijacked his response: instead of calling for help, Samir adopted a fawn response, becoming overly compliant and apologetic to the anesthesiologist until the panic subsided. This maladaptive strategy, combined with his growing belief that the world was fundamentally unpredictable, drove him to avoid going out entirely. He began calling in sick, rationalizing that if he stayed indoors and pretended the event hadn't been that severe, he might eventually stop feeling terrified. However, this avoidance only intensified his physiological scanning. By refusing to leave his apartment, his nervous system remained stuck in a defensive loop, making every minor noise feel like a precursor to violence. The more he tried to dismiss the trauma, the more his negative appraisals hardened, convincing him that he had to be especially careful because danger was inevitable. These beliefs, in turn, kept his memory systems hypersensitive; his mind braced for threat so constantly that it misfired, turning ordinary stimuli into full traumatic recalls. The isolation strained his relationship, and the weight of his unprocessed symptoms finally forced him into our intake office. He had come to believe that his former optimism was gone, replaced by a relentless need to monitor his surroundings for danger. What frightened him most was that his avoidance had made him a ghost in his own career, leaving him uncertain if he could ever return to treating animals or trusting his own perception of reality. He sat now, hands folded tightly in his lap, hoping for a way to untangle the memories without losing his livelihood, and dreading the thought that his hypervigilance might never quiet down.

output.rationale: The vignette conveys causal links for 11 edges, notably memory driving appraisals and threat, and maladaptive strategies reinforcing appraisals and threat.
